name: youtube-comments-api
h1: Export YouTube Comments Without Usernames — for Sentiment and Research
metaTitle: Export YouTube Comments, No Usernames | ActorForge
metaDescription: Export YouTube comments and replies via the official API, with commenter names, IDs and avatars stripped. Ideal for sentiment analysis. $0.50 per 1,000.
tagline: Comment text, likes, reply counts and dates for any video, with every commenter's name, channel ID and avatar removed before the data reaches you.
intro: When you analyse YouTube comments, the useful part is what people said, not who said it. Yet most comment exports hand you display names, channel IDs and profile pictures, which turns a sentiment dataset into a list of identifiable people you then have to manage. This actor strips those fields from every row by design.

It reads comments through the official **YouTube Data API v3** with your own free API key. Each row holds the comment text, like count, reply count, published and edited dates, comment ID and video ID. Turn on `includeReplies` to add replies as their own rows, linked to the parent by `parentId` and capped by `maxRepliesPerComment` (default 20), so one enormous thread cannot consume the run.

It fits sentiment analysis, audience research, product feedback mining, LLM and RAG datasets and moderation reviews. Comments cost $0.50 per 1,000, and one free key covers about 1 million comments a day. If you need to know who commented, this is deliberately not the tool for that.
howItWorks: Video URLs or IDs are read from `videoUrls` and comment threads are fetched with `commentThreads.list`, 100 per call.
Top-level comments are capped per video by `maxCommentsPerVideo`, sorted newest first or by YouTube's top comments via `commentOrder`.
With `includeReplies` on, up to 5 replies come with each thread call, and longer threads are fetched with `comments.list` up to `maxRepliesPerComment`.
Author display name, channel ID, profile image and channel URL are removed from every row before it is written to your dataset.
Videos with comments turned off, or that are private or deleted, produce a free error row.

useCases.title: Sentiment analysis on a launch video
useCases.text: Export the top or newest comments on a product launch, trailer or ad and score them with your own model. Because author fields are gone, the dataset is just text, likes and timestamps.

useCases.title: Training and RAG datasets
useCases.text: Collect comment text across many videos for classification, topic modelling or retrieval experiments without storing commenter identities alongside it. Remember that @mentions typed inside a comment stay in the text.

useCases.title: Product feedback mining
useCases.text: Use `searchTerms` to have YouTube return only comments containing a keyword, such as a feature name or a bug, then read or cluster just those.

useCases.title: Moderation and community review
useCases.text: Pull the newest comments with `commentOrder` set to time on a schedule and review them in a spreadsheet, using like and reply counts to prioritise.

comparisonNote: If your project genuinely needs to know who commented, or whether the creator pinned or hearted a comment, a scraper that keeps author fields is the better fit. This actor is for work where the text matters and the identities are a liability.

faq.q: How can I export YouTube comments to CSV for sentiment analysis?
faq.a: Add the video links to `videoUrls`, pick how many top-level comments you want with `maxCommentsPerVideo`, and run. The dataset can be downloaded as CSV, JSON or Excel, with one row per comment and no author fields.

faq.q: Does the export include commenter usernames?
faq.a: No. Display name, author channel ID, profile image and channel URL are stripped from every row. The comment text is returned as written, so an @mention someone typed stays in the text.

faq.q: Are replies counted against the comment limit?
faq.a: No. `maxCommentsPerVideo` counts top-level comments only. Replies are capped per thread by `maxRepliesPerComment` (default 20, 0 for none, up to 1,000), and each reply is its own billed row.

faq.q: How many YouTube comments can I download per day?
faq.a: Comment threads cost 1 quota unit per 100 comments, so the 10,000 free daily units on one key cover about 1 million comments. Long reply threads use 1 extra unit per 100 replies beyond the first 5.

faq.q: What happens if a video has comments turned off?
faq.a: You get a free error row for that video and the run continues with the others. Nothing is charged for it.
